Serving: rcp-ndcg-vllm's folded model plugin (the one vllm.general_plugins entry point)
(rcp-ndcg-vllm/plugins/pplx/, pure Python, installed with pip install
--no-deps into the unmodified image) registers the checkpoint's
PplxContextualModel as a pooling model: the language_model.* weight mapper,
the contextual_projection head, and a chunk pooler that segments on the
boundary id 248079 and applies the int8 tanh head. It also registers the
checkpoint's transformers config class (hf_config.PplxContextualConfig, the
remote configuration class restated field for field), so --trust-remote-code
is unnecessary and the remote config module never executes. The plugin must
NOT register a multimodal processor (the ColQwen3_5 precedent it is modelled
on does): the embedding code is text-only, and a copy-paste would silently
embed images into a text model instead of rejecting them.

The wire contract (request_shape: token_ids). The reference tokenizes the
document with split_special_tokens=True, so the reference's document ids open
with the two literal tokens that the "[D] " string renders under that parse
(ids 62724, 60) while a server-side parse of the same text keeps the added
special id 248078 (measured at the pinned revision: 27 vs 26 tokens, divergence
at index 0); the boundary marker is a NON-special added token and keeps its one
id 248079 in both parses. The plugin implements the reference's id space and
refuses inputs whose first id is neither 248077 (the query prefix) nor
(62724, 60): queries are [248077] + tokenize(query); documents are the split
render of "[D] " + chunks joined by the boundary marker, with 248079 markers
and the prefix and markers excluded from every pooled span.

PRODUCT GAP (reported, not worked around): the product's token-ids route
tokenises the fitted render with the tokenizer's ADDED-TOKEN parse, which
opens a document with the one special id 248078 where the reference's
document ids open with (62724, 60) -- and the two parses' first content
pretoken differs as well (the measured 0..+2-token prefix delta). Queries
match the reference ids over that route (measured: [248077] + body equals the
remote's prepend construction). Documents therefore diverge at the prefix
boundary and the plugin REFUSES them loudly, so stage 2 can verify the query
leg today and cannot verify documents until the product's id derivation can
request the reference's split parse (a tokenizer parse mode on the ids path
-- transformers' split_special_tokens is the raw tokenizers
encode_special_tokens toggle -- consumed by the pooling client's token-id
derivation). Token ids stay the declared wire: it is the only route that can
carry the reference ids at all. The declared render TEXT is byte-identical to
the reference's on both shapes (stage 1 proves it), so the id-derivation seam
is the whole remaining delta.

Role disambiguation on the engine (the plugin's rule): first id 248077 -> query, pooled as the mean over
the whole sequence with the prefix token included; leading (62724, 60) ->
document, pooled as one span mean per chunk between 248079 markers, the
prefix and the markers excluded from every span. A one-chunk document has no
marker and is a single span; the leading id is the only role signal. An empty
chunk (consecutive or trailing markers) pools to the zero vector, the
reference's own branch for a chunk with no tokens.

Chunks: the document content is the model's chunk list joined by the boundary
marker - chunk boundaries are input to this model, and the chunker that
produces them is declared preprocessing recorded upstream of this recipe. A
chunk's text must contain no all-special token of this tokenizer; the
boundary marker is the declared case (the plugin segments on every 248079, so
a marker inside chunk text would create phantom chunks), and the reference's split-side parse makes
any other all-special token in content diverge from the engine-side parse the
same way. reference.py re-splits the content on the marker for the model call.

Scores: the card gives per-chunk scores (doc_embeddings @ query_embeddings)
but no aggregation; the product's multi-vector scorer (MaxSim with a single
query vector) pools by max over chunks. Max is the retrieval reading and
INFERENCE - the GPU wave confirms it against the vendor's retrieval numbers.

dtype: vLLM v0.31.0 cannot run this model in float32: the GDN prefill kernels
refuse it on every backend (flashinfer's _cutlass_io_dtype raises
"Unsupported dtype torch.float32, expected bfloat16 or float16", observed both at
kernel warmup and on the first forward when the checkpoint was served in float32 on
the stock v0.31.0 image; the Triton/FLA path
asserts "ChunkGatedDeltaRuleFunction does not support float32. Please use
bfloat16.", third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/chunk.py:213-215 at the
tag). The recipe therefore serves dtype: bfloat16 (16.8 GB of weights; the
33,604,334,528-byte fp32 checkpoint is cast at load) while the REFERENCE
runs the checkpoint's own fp32 (the card's AutoModel.from_pretrained passes
no dtype, so the config's float32 loads) -- the served-vs-reference difference is the
cast plus the kernels, and stage 2's tolerance gate and the wave's retrieval
numbers quantify it. The first equivalence plan's float32 rung is deleted:
it is unservable on this engine. The int8 head stays fp32 on both sides (the
remote code's _keep_in_fp32_modules; the plugin's head_dtype). Skipping the
unused vision tower saves 1.82 GB fp32 (parsed from the checkpoint's shard
headers).

Budget: the model's own limit is 262144 tokens model-side (config
query_length and document_length; the model raises beyond it and truncates
nothing). The model-side count of a render is the engine-side count plus a
content-dependent prefix delta: the [D] prefix contributes +1 (two literal
ids where the engine-side count keeps one special id) minus whatever the
first content pretoken saves by re-tokenizing with the prefix's trailing
space - measured total deltas 0..+2 over letter, digit, whitespace, CJK and
emoji-initial content, worst 2. The client budget is therefore
262142: the measured worst case reserved, so no measured render hits the
model's own raise, and a content class outside the measured ones fails
loudly at the engine's own max_model_len, never silently. The pooling role
client fits every request to the declared tokenizer and budget before it
derives the token ids (rcp-ndcg/src/rcp_ndcg/inference/clients/pool.py: content-only
cuts, every cut census-recorded): the cut is the declared policy. The model card
has no over-limit output to compare with (it raises), so the pairs files keep
every text under the limit; reference.py's render of such a row is the uncut
prompt, which stage 1 reports as a mismatch. max_model_len
262144 reserves whole-sequence prefill (bidirectional pooling disables
chunked prefill at the pinned engine): roughly 8.5 GB of bf16 KV per 262k
sequence (the GDN state cache stays fp32 via mamba_ssm_dtype, small beside
it). The wave confirms the VRAM plan and lowers BOTH numbers deliberately,
never one, if the slot cannot afford the worst case.

golden:
Frame: the model reads every input through its chat template - a system turn carrying the instruction, a user turn carrying the content, then the assistant header; the pooled token is the tokenizer post-processor's endoftext (id 151643) appended after it. The card frames a query exactly like a document: every usage example encodes queries without an instruction of their own, so the default "Represent the user's input." applies to both sides (format_model_input; the sentence-transformers prompts.default). The template therefore declares a query shape and a document shape with the same frame; the recipe's test renders the checkpoint's own chat_template.jinja at the pinned revision (hash-pinned) for one query and one document and requires both declared shapes to render the same strings. No template file ships (serve.chat_template null): every item rides the messages route as one conversation carrying its content only, and the engine frames it with the checkpoint's own chat_template.jinja - its default system message is the card's instruction, and with add_generation_prompt true (sent; vLLM's chat routes default it to false) it closes with the assistant header, so the engine's render is the declared frame, once; add_special_tokens true (sent) appends the endoftext anchor. The harness's template check reads that checkpoint file at the pinned revision and renders it over every conversation the client sends. A custom instruction is a different serving mode - a new template and judgement family, not this recipe (the pairs files carry no instruction field, and the reference refuses rows that carry one). The card's empty-input rule renders the text NULL, hence empty_doc: send_text "NULL": the client decides on the content before the frame, so an empty document ships NULL inside the user turn, as the card renders it. No query_max_tokens: the card caps the WHOLE prompt (MAX_LENGTH 8192) for both sides alike, mirrored by client.max_tokens.
Budgets: client.max_tokens is the declared policy, reserved frame-first with the content span cut (on_overflow: cut) and an item's media tokens reserved whole beside it; the embed client fits every request to it before shipping. The card's own truncation (the processor's truncation=True at max_length 8192) right-cuts the whole prompt: the frame's tail is cut and only the post-processor's endoftext is re-appended - the declared anchor_drop_over_cap deviation. reference.py renders exactly that cut (by character offsets on the rendered prompt, never a decode). The harness reports, in stage 1 and stage 2 alike, every text the client changed (its processing record: a budget cut counted with the frame) in the non-gating table under the declared deviation, and gates every other text exactly.
Media (the pixel pin). Serve: serve.mm_processor_kwargs pins {min_pixels: 4096, max_pixels: 1843200} under the nested images_kwargs scope - ONE shape across the media recipes, decided from the v0.31.0 tag source: the nested dict reaches the HF processor's images_kwargs (and through it the resize) and the vLLM-side image token budget, while the flat form also re-sizes every video clip (see sources). The checkpoint's own default is 4096..1310720 px (preprocessor_config.json), so the pin is load-bearing: unpinned, a page the client prepares above 1310720 px is resized again and counts other tokens. Capacity: one media item per request (serve.limit_mm_per_prompt image=1 video=1; client.max_images and max_videos carry the same numbers). Client half: image_processor qwen3_vl and client.image_policy with the same pixel numbers and engine_pixel_pinning true - the declaration that admits the card's 4096 px floor below the family's stock 65536 px - so the client resizes every image exactly as the card's fetch_image does (qwen-vl-utils smart_resize, factor 32) and counts it as the engine does. Media ride the messages route only, each item its own conversation, media before text (the card's format_model_input order). The harness's media stage holds the client's sent images (count, placement, prepared geometry, tokens) to reference.py --mode media and, against the engine, the engine's media count to the client's; the negative control that unpins the budget fails it (the pin's 1843200 px ceiling leaves the checkpoint's own 1310720).

golden:
What the model is. A multimodal late-interaction (multi-vector) retriever: one L2-normalized
2048-dim vector per kept token, retrieval score = fp32 MaxSim, client-side. Text prompts are NOT
chat-formatted: raw "Query: " + text.strip() and "Document: " + (text).strip() (topk_embed_st.py:56-60,
format_query/format_document; the strings are config.json:104-105). Image documents go through the
checkpoint's chat template as an image-ONLY user message (no text part): a text part alongside the
image changes the prompt ids (measured).
The recipe's template declares both text shapes; the image shape is the product's pooling-chat path
(media items travel as messages, where the server applies the model's chat template and expands the
single image placeholder to ceil(H/32)*ceil(W/32) patch tokens -- the same formula as
topk_embed_st.py:121-122.

The served vs reference rendering contract (stage 1):
- query shape: "Query: " + query text; every query token keeps its vector (punctuation included).
- document shape: "Document: " + document; every token NOT in scoring_skip_ids keeps its vector
  (config.json:107-148: 41 ids = 32 standalone ASCII punctuation single-char tokens + 9 special
  tokens). The filter is load-bearing for plain prose (the sample pair's document drops 4 positions,
  including the prompt's own colon token).
- Content normalisation (template.normalize: [strip]): the model's wrapper strips the query text on
  both sides and the whole document RENDER. The declared per-span strip reproduces the query render
  byte-for-byte on every input, and the document render on every input except two corners the span
  rule cannot express: (a) document content with LEADING whitespace -- the reference's whole-render
  strip keeps it (the frame's own leading text), the content-span strip removes it; (b) empty or
  whitespace-only content -- the reference renders "Document:" (see 'Empty documents'). Both corners
  are declared divergence rows: the stage-1 render check flags exactly these inputs, and the wave's
  pairs must not sample them.
- The image wrapper is pinned by the recipe's test at the pinned revision: the chat template's
  image-only user message renders to [im_start, "user", newline, vision_start] + one image
  placeholder + [vision_end, end-of-turn, newline] (ids 248045, 846, 198, 248053, 248056*N,
  248054, 248046, 198).

Why chat_template is null: the checkpoint SHIPS chat_template.jinja at the pinned
revision and vLLM resolves it through AutoProcessor for the pooling-chat (media) path; a missing
template there is a loud per-request error (ChatTemplateResolutionError), never the silent
warn-and-concatenate fallback -- that fallback lives in the scoring io-processor
(pooling/scoring/io_processor.py:677-678), which this recipe does not use. Shipping a copy would add
a second source of truth for a file the engine already pins through the revision. The harness's
stage-1 template check cannot render a messages-based template (it renders query/document
variables), so the recipe's test pins the image wrapper structure directly instead. The GPU wave's
T0 probe-image check (the prompt-token count of one probe image) proves the engine loaded the
checkpoint's template.

The declared fields that make the card's behaviour expressible with the product:
- The document keep-mask -> client.document_skip_token_ids (the 41 ids above): the client drops the
  document-side vectors at the ids it sent and cross-checks the returned counts. The skip rule at image
  positions (workstream 09): a media document rides the messages route and the client KEEPS every
  returned vector of one (a media request's positions are the server's chat-template render, which the
  client cannot tokenise -- the image positions are exempt, never skipped), and the deviation is recorded
  on the row's processing record (skip_unapplied). The reference's IMAGE documents keep only the
  image-patch positions (topk_embed_st.py:124), so a served image document's vector set is a superset of
  the reference's keep-mask (the frame text stays): image documents are sendable and the media stage
  verifies their geometry and tokens, while scoring them against the reference stays a declared
  approximation until a corpus observes the kept positions.
- Per-role caps -> client.query_max_tokens 1024 beside client.max_tokens 8192: queries are cut at
  the model's own query_length on every path, documents at document_length; both cuts are the
  product's fit (content span only, the fixed head reserved, census-recorded).
- Per-role input -> client.media_sides: ["document"]: the reference rejects image queries and so
  does the client (a typed refusal naming the field, before the media is fetched).
- The content strip -> template.normalize: [strip] (see the rendering contract above for the two
  declared corners).
- The counting ceiling is fixed in the product: the checkpoint's tokenizer.json embeds
  truncation {Right, 1024}, and the product's TextTokenizer.from_json resets the backend's embedded
  truncation and padding at load -- exactly what transformers does per call -- so counting, id
  lists and offsets run past 1024 tokens to the true budget. Stage 1 was re-run with over-length
  inputs above 1024 tokens (query samples over 1024, document samples over 8192): the anchor audit
  and the render check pass there, and the fit cuts them at the declared caps.

Budget: max_tokens 8192 is the document cap and query_max_tokens 1024 the query cap -- each the
shape's whole rendered prompt as the engine sees it, in the tokenizer's tokens, right truncation
(the wrapper passes explicit max_length to the processor). on_overflow: cut: the content span only,
the fixed head reserved, the template re-attached (the product's fit, one budget per shape). The
card's own cut (topk_embed_st.py:75-77: the processor's truncation=True at max_length 1024 for
queries, 8192 for documents) right-cuts the formatted prompt's ids; reference.py renders exactly that
cut, located by character offsets. Both cuts keep the fixed head and keep the same text on every
input measured (English, punctuation-heavy, CJK, emoji and repeated-letter content), but the card
cuts ids, not text: when its last kept id lands inside a character spanning several byte-level
tokens (an emoji), the card's model reads that character's leading bytes, which no text carries --
one more id than the client sends. Hence over_cap_cut_differs (the anchor kept, the kept content
differing by that id; a stage-2 difference, the render texts are equal). What the harness does today: stage 1 treats a row as over cap
only when a cut's content tokens exceed client.max_tokens (8192), so a document row whose content
alone exceeds 8192 tokens is reported, not gated, while a document that overflows only with the
head and every query cut at its 1024 share are gated. Stage 1 passes on them (equal texts); stage 2
would gate a split-character row's vectors. The wave's pairs files must keep queries within 1024
tokens and documents within 8192.

Empty documents: the reference renders an empty document as "Document:" -- exactly one kept token
(the colon is a skip id), so the wrapper's `or eos or "."` fallback is dead code for this
checkpoint (the stripped render is never empty), and the reference scores MaxSim against that one
vector. The schema cannot express that render (the frame's trailing space cannot be stripped), and
the alternatives diverge differently (`empty_doc: send` renders "Document: ", two kept tokens),
so the recipe declares `empty_doc: omit_zero` -- never sent, scored 0.0 -- as a recorded
approximation, and the wave's pairs must not sample empty documents.

Media (the pixel pin, both halves): serve.mm_processor_kwargs pins min_pixels 65536 / max_pixels 1310720 -- the reference's
image budget (topk_embed_st.py:36-37: shortest_edge and image_token_budget 1280 * (16*2)^2). The
client declares the same numbers (image_processor qwen3_vl, image_policy 65536..1310720,
max_images 1, media_sides documents-only), so the client half holds: the client resizes and
counts images exactly as the processor would within that budget. The shipped processor_config
allows 16,777,216 px (processor_config.json:23), about 16k image tokens, so the override is
load-bearing for both sides. The pin rides the ONE shape decided for the media recipes from the
v0.31.0 tag source, nested images_kwargs: the nested dict reaches the HF processor's
images_kwargs (the resize) and the vLLM-side image token budget alike, and never the video
path (see sources). The wave's T0 probe (one image, usage.prompt_tokens <= 4 + 1280 + 3)
measures the served count.

Reference: sentence-transformers 6.0.1 MultiVectorEncoder over the checkpoint's trusted code --
the model card's own published path (config_sentence_transformers.json: model_type
MultiVectorEncoder, similarity MaxSim; modules.json: topk_embed_st.TopkEmbedTransformer). Its
environment is the checkpoint's requirements.txt pins, declared in requirements-reference.txt
(torch 2.11.0, torchvision 0.26.0, transformers 5.9.0, sentence-transformers 6.0.1,

loudly.

golden:
What the model is. A multimodal late-interaction (multi-vector) retriever: one L2-normalized
2048-dim vector per kept token, retrieval score = fp32 MaxSim, client-side. Text prompts are NOT
chat-formatted: raw "Query: " + text.strip() and "Document: " + (text).strip() (topk_embed_st.py:56-60,
format_query/format_document; the strings are config.json:104-105). Image documents go through the
checkpoint's chat template as an image-ONLY user message (no text part): a text part alongside the
image changes the prompt ids (measured).
The recipe's template declares both text shapes; the image shape is the product's pooling-chat path
(media items travel as messages, where the server applies the model's chat template and expands the
single image placeholder to ceil(H/32)*ceil(W/32) patch tokens -- the same formula as
topk_embed_st.py:121-122.

The served vs reference rendering contract (stage 1):
- query shape: "Query: " + query text; every query token keeps its vector (punctuation included).
- document shape: "Document: " + document; every token NOT in scoring_skip_ids keeps its vector
  (config.json:107-148: 41 ids = 32 standalone ASCII punctuation single-char tokens + 9 special
  tokens). The filter is load-bearing for plain prose (the sample pair's document drops 4 positions,
  including the prompt's own colon token).
- Content normalisation (template.normalize: [strip]): the model's wrapper strips the query text on
  both sides and the whole document RENDER. The declared per-span strip reproduces the query render
  byte-for-byte on every input, and the document render on every input except two corners the span
  rule cannot express: (a) document content with LEADING whitespace -- the reference's whole-render
  strip keeps it (the frame's own leading text), the content-span strip removes it; (b) empty or
  whitespace-only content -- the reference renders "Document:" (see 'Empty documents'). Both corners
  are declared divergence rows: the stage-1 render check flags exactly these inputs, and the wave's
  pairs must not sample them.
- The image wrapper is pinned by the recipe's test at the pinned revision: the chat template's
  image-only user message renders to [im_start, "user", newline, vision_start] + one image
  placeholder + [vision_end, end-of-turn, newline] (ids 248045, 846, 198, 248053, 248056*N,
  248054, 248046, 198).

Why chat_template is null: the checkpoint SHIPS chat_template.jinja at the pinned
revision and vLLM resolves it through AutoProcessor for the pooling-chat (media) path; a missing
template there is a loud per-request error (ChatTemplateResolutionError), never the silent
warn-and-concatenate fallback -- that fallback lives in the scoring io-processor
(pooling/scoring/io_processor.py:677-678), which this recipe does not use. Shipping a copy would add
a second source of truth for a file the engine already pins through the revision. The harness's
stage-1 template check cannot render a messages-based template (it renders query/document
variables), so the recipe's test pins the image wrapper structure directly instead. The GPU wave's
T0 probe-image check (the prompt-token count of one probe image) proves the engine loaded the
checkpoint's template.

The declared fields that make the card's behaviour expressible with the product:
- The document keep-mask -> client.document_skip_token_ids (the 41 ids above): the client drops the
  document-side vectors at the ids it sent and cross-checks the returned counts. The skip rule at image
  positions (workstream 09): a media document rides the messages route and the client KEEPS every
  returned vector of one (a media request's positions are the server's chat-template render, which the
  client cannot tokenise -- the image positions are exempt, never skipped), and the deviation is recorded
  on the row's processing record (skip_unapplied). The reference's IMAGE documents keep only the
  image-patch positions (topk_embed_st.py:124), so a served image document's vector set is a superset of
  the reference's keep-mask (the frame text stays): image documents are sendable and the media stage
  verifies their geometry and tokens, while scoring them against the reference stays a declared
  approximation until a corpus observes the kept positions.
- Per-role caps -> client.query_max_tokens 1024 beside client.max_tokens 8192: queries are cut at
  the model's own query_length on every path, documents at document_length; both cuts are the
  product's fit (content span only, the fixed head reserved, census-recorded).
- Per-role input -> client.media_sides: ["document"]: the reference rejects image queries and so
  does the client (a typed refusal naming the field, before the media is fetched).
- The content strip -> template.normalize: [strip] (see the rendering contract above for the two
  declared corners).
- The counting ceiling is fixed in the product: the checkpoint's tokenizer.json embeds
  truncation {Right, 1024}, and the product's TextTokenizer.from_json resets the backend's embedded
  truncation and padding at load -- exactly what transformers does per call -- so counting, id
  lists and offsets run past 1024 tokens to the true budget. Stage 1 was re-run with over-length
  inputs above 1024 tokens (query samples over 1024, document samples over 8192): the anchor audit
  and the render check pass there, and the fit cuts them at the declared caps.

Budget: max_tokens 8192 is the document cap and query_max_tokens 1024 the query cap -- each the
shape's whole rendered prompt as the engine sees it, in the tokenizer's tokens, right truncation
(the wrapper passes explicit max_length to the processor). on_overflow: cut: the content span only,
the fixed head reserved, the template re-attached (the product's fit, one budget per shape). The
card's own cut (topk_embed_st.py:75-77: the processor's truncation=True at max_length 1024 for
queries, 8192 for documents) right-cuts the formatted prompt's ids; reference.py renders exactly that
cut, located by character offsets. Both cuts keep the fixed head and keep the same text on every
input measured (English, punctuation-heavy, CJK, emoji and repeated-letter content), but the card
cuts ids, not text: when its last kept id lands inside a character spanning several byte-level
tokens (an emoji), the card's model reads that character's leading bytes, which no text carries --
one more id than the client sends. Hence over_cap_cut_differs (the anchor kept, the kept content
differing by that id; a stage-2 difference, the render texts are equal). What the harness does today: stage 1 treats a row as over cap
only when a cut's content tokens exceed client.max_tokens (8192), so a document row whose content
alone exceeds 8192 tokens is reported, not gated, while a document that overflows only with the
head and every query cut at its 1024 share are gated. Stage 1 passes on them (equal texts); stage 2
would gate a split-character row's vectors. The wave's pairs files must keep queries within 1024
tokens and documents within 8192.

Empty documents: the reference renders an empty document as "Document:" -- exactly one kept token
(the colon is a skip id), so the wrapper's `or eos or "."` fallback is dead code for this
checkpoint (the stripped render is never empty), and the reference scores MaxSim against that one
vector. The schema cannot express that render (the frame's trailing space cannot be stripped), and
the alternatives diverge differently (`empty_doc: send` renders "Document: ", two kept tokens),
so the recipe declares `empty_doc: omit_zero` -- never sent, scored 0.0 -- as a recorded
approximation, and the wave's pairs must not sample empty documents.

Media (the pixel pin, both halves): serve.mm_processor_kwargs pins min_pixels 65536 / max_pixels 1310720 -- the reference's
image budget (topk_embed_st.py:36-37: shortest_edge and image_token_budget 1280 * (16*2)^2). The
client declares the same numbers (image_processor qwen3_vl, image_policy 65536..1310720,
max_images 1, media_sides documents-only), so the client half holds: the client resizes and
counts images exactly as the processor would within that budget. The shipped processor_config
allows 16,777,216 px (processor_config.json:23), about 16k image tokens, so the override is
load-bearing for both sides. The pin rides the ONE shape decided for the media recipes from the
v0.31.0 tag source, nested images_kwargs: the nested dict reaches the HF processor's
images_kwargs (the resize) and the vLLM-side image token budget alike, and never the video
path (see sources). The wave's T0 probe (one image, usage.prompt_tokens <= 4 + 1280 + 3)
measures the served count.

the model card's own published path (config_sentence_transformers.json: model_type

Serving: vllm serve zeroentropy/zembed-1-embedding --runner pooling --convert embed
--max-model-len 32768, on the unmodified vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0 image, no plugin.
1. Runner/convert are explicit for robustness: at v0.31.0 a bare serve already resolves this
   checkpoint to pooling + embed, because the sentence-transformers modules.json wins over the
   generative Qwen3ForCausalLM architecture and convert falls through to embed for a pooling
   runner on a CausalLM arch. The flags equal what auto resolves; they pin the intent.
2. pooler_config stays empty on purpose: the engine reads modules.json + 1_Pooling/config.json
   (last-token pooling, L2 normalize) from the checkpoint itself, and the embed conversion
   normalizes server-side. There is no chat template on the serving path: the prompts are
   literal client-side text, the checkpoint's own chat_template.jinja stays unused, and
   serve.chat_template is null. Never route this model through /v2/embed with input_type: that
   route renders chat messages through the Qwen3 chat template, a different token sequence
   (measured when the recipe was written). The engine never imports the remote module, so trust_remote_code is false.
3. The render is prefix + content + suffix, declared as data in client.template: the query and
   document prompts come from config_sentence_transformers.json, and the suffix (the im_end
   marker plus a newline) is appended by the checkpoint's remote code (modeling_zembed.py:13,
   ZembedTransformer.tokenize). The suffix is load-bearing: the pooler reads the last token, so
   it is the template's trailing fixed segment and the anchor the budget reserves. The template
   writes specials by name ({special:im_start}, {special:im_end}), never literally.
4. Budget: the whole rendered prompt is capped at 32768 tokens (sentence_bert_config.json
   max_seq_length, the same number as serve.max_model_len). on_overflow: cut trims the content
   spans only, after reserving every fixed template token, and re-attaches the frame, so the
   anchor survives every cut (docs/how-to/add-a-model.md, "Anchors"). The engine never truncates: vLLM
   defaults to no truncation and 400s over-length inputs, so the client-side cut (the merged
   product's embedding client fitting every request to the declared budget,
   rcp_ndcg.data.preprocess.fit) is the only one. Per-shape query caps (whether
   query_max_tokens applies): no separate query cap exists in the referent - the reference cuts
   queries and documents alike at 32768 tokens - so query_max_tokens is not declared and both
   shapes draw on max_tokens.
5. The reference is the model's published path verbatim and never ports the client's cut
   (docs/how-to/add-a-model.md): over-cap, the remote tokenize's whole-prompt right cut drops the
   pooled suffix token, while the served side keeps the anchor
   by the declared client cut. The reference's over-cap cut therefore differs from the client's
   AND drops the anchor, so the recipe declares reference.known_deviations: [anchor_drop_over_cap]:
   over-cap pairs ride the non-gating table and stage 2 gates only the under-cap rows.
6. Dimensions: 2560 only. The card's smaller sizes (1280..40) come from projections.safetensors
   - six chained learned F32 matrices (4,368,000 params; params x 4 B + 456 B header =
   17,472,456 B exactly) - not Matryoshka slices, and no public code loads them. The checkpoint
   declares no matryoshka_dimensions, so vLLM refuses a dimensions parameter outright; do not
   set client.dimensions for this model.
7. Reference environment (the reference's own python, per requirements-reference.txt):
   torch>=2.0, transformers>=4.51 (Qwen3's floor; the image's transformers serves it), numpy,
   and sentence-transformers>=5.3,<5.4 -- the last line whose encode calls the remote
   tokenize; from 5.4.0 the preprocess-first pipeline bypasses the tokenize-only remote module
   and silently drops the suffix. 5.1.x would require transformers<5 and could not reuse the
   image's transformers (>=5.10.4,<5.18.0 at v0.31.0); 5.3.x accepts it, so the reference venv
   (--system-site-packages over the image) installs only sentence-transformers. The reference loads the checkpoint with trust_remote_code=True (the model card's
   usage); the served engine never imports that code.
8. Status unverified: the render was proved token-exact on CPU (8/8 cases measured when the recipe was written,
   constants bound to the checkpoint's config files); vector-level equivalence, the engine's
   /tokenize check and the bf16-head/fp32-normalize drift (expected ~1e-3, within the 1-1e-3
   vector gate) all need the GPU wave.
